subject: Edge segment shadowing: bonded-switch NAT + MTU playbook
messages:
From: Jason Liu <jason.liu@acmetech.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: network_ops@acmetech.com
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent upload failures across on-prem edge segment

Hi Rafael / Monica,

We started seeing intermittent failures when bulk-uploading (S3 over VPN) from our on-prem cluster connected via the new bonded edge switch. The flows succeed for small objects but larger uploads stall at ~36KB chunks. TCP retransmits and sometimes the client retries resolve it. We captured a few PCAPs and an ifconfig output from the SVI — attaching both.

Observed details:
- Failures only for hosts in VLAN 214 (bridged across two physical switches)
- Bonded pair on the edge appears to be LACP active-active
- NAT entries on Redwood's appliance show 1:many mapping on one physical uplink and not the other
- When we temporarily lower MTU on the host (to 1400) the issue disappears

Can you advise next steps? This is impacting nightly backups and needs a short remediation/playbook so our ops team can run it with minimal handholding.

Thanks,
Jason Liu
Network Engineer, AcmeTech

Attachment stubs: packet-capture-20250514.pcap (pcap), ifconfig-sv1.txt (text)
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Jason Liu <jason.liu@acmetech.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent upload failures across on-prem edge segment

Thanks Jason — and sorry you're seeing this. We're opening an escalation and drafting an actionable playbook you can run. Quick notes from first pass:

1) Symptom points to MTU/fragmentation or asymmetric NAT across bonded uplinks. The fact that lowering MTU helps strongly suggests a fragmentation or path-MTU blackhole.
2) LACP active-active with asymmetric hashing can cause return traffic to take a different physical uplink than outbound; if your NAT appliance pins state to a specific IP:port tied to an uplink, replies can be dropped or re-associated incorrectly.

Proposed short playbook (we'll validate with tests in parallel):
- Step A: On a small subset of hosts in VLAN 214, enable MTU clamp on the SVI/inbound interface to 1400 and run the upload test (confirm behavioral change).
- Step B: On the bonded edge switch, temporarily force the LACP hash to include source/destination ports (makes flows stickier) or set the bond mode to active-backup for a short window for testing.
- Step C: On Redwood side, check NAT affinity: dump conntrack/NAT table to verify mapped entries for the client IPs and which physical uplink they are tied to. If NAT state is present on only one appliance instance, we can either sync state or route both directions through the same instance.
- Step D: Capture packet traces simultaneously on host, switch, and Redwood appliance to correlate SYN/SYN-ACK/fragment paths.

I've looped in Monica (networking lead) and Karthik (private deploy/runtime) to help with packet triage and a temporary config we can push. We'll produce commands and an ops-runbook in the next message.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, Jason Liu <jason.liu@acmetech.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent upload failures across on-prem edge segment

Quick triage notes and exact commands I ran against the captures you sent. I'm pasting outputs inline and attaching my conntrack dump (see ifconfig-sv1.txt + conntrack snippet in attachments).

- I compared the pcap: client sends large segments with DF set, path is MTU-sensitive. SYN goes out via uplink1, SYN-ACK arrives via uplink2 in many traces — asymmetric return.
- Conntrack on the Redwood NAT appliance shows state bound to uplink1 IP for the five affected client ephemeral ports; there are corresponding unmatched fragments arriving on uplink2 that are dropped because the conntrack entry only exists on the instance handling uplink1.

Commands I recommend for your ops run: (please test on a single host)

1) Temporary host-side MTU clamp (Linux):
   sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1400
   # run upload test

2) Switch-side stickiness test (Cisco-ish):
   interface Port-channel1
     port-channel load-balance src-dst-port
   # This biases hashing to include TCP ports so flows are less likely to split

   OR (if risk-acceptable) temporarily set to active-backup:
   interface Port-channel1
     no mode active
     mode on

3) On Redwood NAT appliance (root):
   sudo conntrack -L | grep <client-ip> > conntrack-client.txt
   sudo ip route get <client-ip> from <nat-uplink1-ip>

4) If stickiness restores, we can do a longer-term fix: enable NAT state sync across the two appliance instances (recommended) or ensure hash policy keeps the flows on the same physical uplink.

I'll prepare a concise playbook file and a minimal rollback plan. Attaching: conntrack-dump-raf.txt

—Monica
Monica Patel
Network Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Jason Liu <jason.liu@acmetech.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: network_ops@acmetech.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent upload failures across on-prem edge segment

Team — thanks for the fast turnaround. We ran the steps this morning in the staging VLAN:
- Applied host MTU clamp (eth0=1400) — upload tests succeeded consistently.
- Switched the port-channel to src-dst-port hashing for 3 hours — performance stable.
- Conntrack dump confirmed entries now seen consistently on the same uplink; we still see occasional fragments arriving on the other uplink but those are now non-essential reruns rather than session-breaking.

Next actions from our side: schedule a controlled window to either:
A) enable NAT state sync on the two Redwood appliance instances (preferred long-term); or
B) keep sticky hashing on the switch (low-risk but operationally manual).

Can Redwood draft the short RFC/playbook we can use for the maintenance window? Also please include the rollback steps (how to revert NAT sync or switch hashing) and a smoke-test checklist (small/big upload, packetcapture locations, example conntrack grep).

Once we have that, AcmeTech will coordinate with our change window and sign-off. Appreciate the help.

—Jason
Jason Liu
Network Engineer, AcmeTech
